The ending feels natural, earned, and purposeful. Throughout the story, the themes of impending birth and sudden death are intertwined—from Barbara measuring her belly in the opening line and thinking of the shooter's mother, to her realization that her unborn baby was present in the room during the tragedy. Concluding the story in the car with a mild contraction ("the body's opinion") as they drive away from the synagogue brings the narrative full circle. Her request for Marty to "slow down" because "there's no hurry" provides emotional closure, reflecting a quiet desire to hold onto the safety of the present moment before bringing new life into a jarring, unpredictable world.
